chinese_source: Jiu Tang shu (Old Book of Tang), Nepal (Nipoluo) account; Old Tibetan Annals frame
event: After the usurpation by his uncle Visnugupta, Narendradeva flees to Tibet; the Tibetans re-establish him on the Nepalese throne (641), making Nepal a Tibetan client; Nepal supplies 7,000 troops to Wang Xuance's 648 campaign and the Tangshu describes Narendradeva as reigning king in information current to c. 648
date_raw: Restoration pegged to 641 (Zhenguan 15 era frame; Tibetan annals place the Nepal intervention in the early 640s)
firmness_reason: Event sequence is annalistic and the Tibetan record concurs; the exact year 641 is the standard scholarly peg within 641-643 rather than a year stated in so many words, and the Tangshu narrative compresses the inscriptional Jishnugupta/Dhruvadeva tangle
notes: Campaign case 10 verdict CORRECTED: the vaimsavali chronology supplies no absolute date for this segment; the Tang/Tibetan peg is the only one.
